name: Jones Lang LaSalle Incorporated
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow: a genuine scale platform (global #2, integrated services, contractual management-services base with very high top-client retention, LaSalle investment-management fees) but a people business whose producers can walk, with no pricing-power proof and measured ROIC only around the cost of capital through the cycle (roic_proxy 7.0-12.5% over 2021-25, trough 7.0% in 2023). CBRE, the #1 franchise, was scored 6/10 in this sweep; JLL sits one notch below it. A 7+ moat would need ROIC sustained well above the cost of capital, which the filed history does not show.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

SBC_TAG_RECONCILED: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense exceeds ShareBasedCompensation for FY2018 (0 vs 26,900,000), FY2019 (28,000,000 vs 76,400,000, +172.9%), FY2020 (36,700,000 vs 47,500,000, +29.4%), FY2021 (17,800,000 vs 80,100,000, +350.0%), FY2022 (6,100,000 vs 75,300,000, +1134.4%), FY2023 (3,400,000 vs 74,900,000, +2102.9%), FY2024 (2,300,000 vs 95,100,000, +4034.8%), FY2025 (2,700,000 vs 112,000,000, +4048.1%); the Allocated figure was used — the Share tag carries only part of stock compensation at this filer (a difference under 1% is tag rounding and needs one line in the analysis)
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-19), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: 'Net capital additions - property and equipment' $(215.6) million for FY2025, with $(185.5) million for FY2024 and $(186.9) million for FY2023 in the same statement; MD&A 'Capital Expenditures' section confirms $215.6M (2025) and $185.5M (2024)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 17.94 vs 3-yr median 9.81 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Quality global #2 CRE services franchise, moat 5/10, but Tier D: weighted IRR 7.52% on the 3-yr median owner's-earnings base of $9.81/sh (engine 5.5 now charges the full $112.0M FY2025 stock comp), IV@15% $114.46 vs $305.50 — the 15% hurdle needs ~$114; the TTM base ($21.86/sh) is a cyclical-upswing print whose capex and 10-Q SBC legs are understated, so it is not pinned (a TTM pin reads Tier C by numbers, which the sector-misfit notch would size to D anyway); confidence low.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Scale global platform: #2 CRE services franchise (with CBRE at the top), integrated leasing + capital markets + property/facilities management across ~80 countries - a corporate client can buy the whole stack from one counterparty

Recurring management-services base: Real Estate Management Services is contractual and retention-led (management cited ~99% retention among top clients and ~80% resilient revenue in Q2 2026 materials) - this carried OCF positive through the 2022-23 transaction freeze
Investment Management (LaSalle) AUM fee stream plus brand/trust with the largest owners: ~95% of the top 100 investors and ~50% of the Fortune 500 are clients (company materials)
Data/tech platform (JLL Technologies, AI/data investment funded from the recurring base) raises cross-sell and switching friction for embedded workplace-management clients
moat_against: People business: producers and client relationships can walk to CBRE/Cushman/rivals; no owned asset, network effect or lock-in protects the brokerage fee pool
Measured returns are only around the cost of capital through the cycle: roic_proxy 12.5% (2021), 9.6% (2022), 7.0% (2023), 9.3% (2024), 11.4% (2025) in fundamentals.json - no wide-moat ROIC signature

Transaction revenue (leasing advisory, capital markets) is un-moated cyclicality: OE/share $13.00 (2021), -$1.84 (2022), $5.91 (2023) in the rate shock (engine 5.5 history with the capex override and reconciled SBC)
Thin economics: operating margin ~4-5% of gross revenue (revenue includes large pass-through reimbursables); sophisticated institutional clients negotiate fees hard

overrides.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-19), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: 'Net capital additions - property and equipment' $(215.6) million for FY2025, with $(185.5) million for FY2024 and $(186.9) million for FY2023 in the same statement; MD&A 'Capital Expenditures' section confirms $215.6M (2025) and $185.5M (2024)
